purpose: FALLBACK ONLY. Family-name keywords -> transfer coordinate, for enzymes with no annotated reaction equation. proxy_policy.mechanism_from_reaction() reads the coordinate from the UniProt/Rhea equation and always wins over this file; a family name does not determine transfer chemistry.
rule: coordinate 'adenylate' = nucleophile attacks P-alpha, leaves along Pa--O3A, 1 catalytic Mg2+ (reaction releases AMP + diphosphate). coordinate 'acyl_phosphate' = nucleophile attacks P-gamma, leaves along Pg--O3B, 2 catalytic Mg2+ (reaction releases ADP + phosphate).
calibrated_note: calibrated=true marks the ONLY regime the assay panel calibrated (P-alpha adenylation in the AMP-binding/ANL superfamily). Every other entry is a mechanistic transfer and must not be reported as a validated activity model.
scope_note: Consumed by structural_modeling only (cofold setup + geometry scoring), downstream of discovery. Not an input to candidate retrieval or ranking.
matching: First entry with a keyword contained in the lower-cased family name wins, so order is significant: calibrated entries first, then transfers.

known_unrepresentable.reason: This family contains BOTH coordinates, so no family-level keyword can be correct for it. DdaG (E2JA32) releases AMP + diphosphate -> P-alpha, 1 Mg2+. Its paralogue DdaF (E2JA31) releases ADP + phosphate -> P-gamma, 2 Mg2+. Deliberately absent from 'entries' so the fallback ABSTAINS here instead of being wrong for one of them; these enzymes must be resolved from their annotated reaction.
known_unrepresentable.evidence: UniProt/Rhea catalytic activity for E2JA32 and E2JA31

caution: A family name is not a mechanism. The case above is a worked counterexample: same InterPro family, opposite attacked phosphorus and opposite metal count. Treat every entry here as a last resort.
